IncidentBot: :rotating_light: PAGE: oncall SRE — p99 tail latency spike detected for streaming route /v1/chat/stream (model=redwood-13b-int8-calib-v2). p95=220ms -> 850ms, p99=480ms -> 1300ms, error-rate ~0.8%. Triggered at 2026-03-15T03:22:56Z. Dashboards: https://dash.redwood.example/streams/13b-int8 -> alert id: A-314159

Todd L.: I’m on it — taking primary. What region is this hitting? any customer-impact notes?

IncidentBot: Affected regions: us-west-2 (70%), eu-west-1 (20%), others small. Top route: /v1/chat/stream. Top model variant: redwood-13b-int8-calib-v2. No elevated OOMs reported but batch queue depth increased.

Samir K.: seeing streaming stalls in logs — repeated `KV_CACHE_MISS` spikes and long dequant memcpy times on GPUs. P95 latency bound mostly by decode loop, p99 dominated by dequant+KV lookup. Example stack snippet from a stalled request:
```
[decode] step=generate token=1024 seq=2048 dequant memcpy 0.92s
[kv] lookup idx=5234 wait=0.45s
```

Jin Park: thanks — that matches a calibration job we rolled out last night (calib-v2). It tightened quant thresholds for int8 to improve throughput but might be brittle for long contexts. I’ll check rollout changelog.

Maria G.: Nora (CS) flagged a ticket — customers in EU experience repeated partial stream frames and client reconnects. CS ticket #CS-8674. We got a few angry messages. Impact: degraded streaming experience for ~10 sessions in last 10m, some retried automatically.

Todd L.: ok, immediate mitigation options: 1) route traffic for /v1/chat/stream to fp16 variant (redwood-13b-fp16-stable) 2) rollback quant calib profile to previous v1 3) temporarily disable prefix/KV caching for long-context sessions 4) increase autoscale ondedicated pool. Prefer 1 or 2 for fastest reduction in tail. Any objections?

Samir K.: prefer option 2 (rollback calib) + route fallback for regions with highest impact. Rollback is quick: `platform rollback --model redwood-13b-int8 --profile calib-v1` should be safe. If rollback not immediate, route to fp16.

eng-runtime: executing a controlled traffic shift to fallback model for us-west-2. Command: `redwood route set --route /v1/chat/stream --model redwood-13b-fp16-stable --weight 100 --region us-west-2 --reason "temp-mitigation-calib-v2"`

Todd L.: doing the rollback now for the global calibration profile. Running: `platform rollback --model redwood-13b-int8 --from calib-v2 --to calib-v1 --no-drain` — will watch disk and GPU mem stats.

Samir K.: monitoring kernel metrics, also toggling aggressive-batching=false for affected pools to reduce queueing. That should help with tail queuing.

Jin Park: FYI the calib-v2 job changed dequant reorder and enabled a faster but untested memcpy path on Ampere chips. Looks like on certain sequence-length distributions (>1024) it causes memcpy stalls during KV warmups. Noted in internal change #CHG-2026-431.

Nora (CS): any ETA to reduce visible customer impact? updates to ticket?

Maria G.: I'll update CS-8674: "Eng investigating. Temporary routing change applied to us-west-2; rollback in progress; expect improvement in 10-15m. We will follow up once stable."

IncidentBot: rollback job started by Todd L. — job id RB-314159-01. Expected propagation 60-120s per node.

eng-runtime: fp16 routing applied to us-west-2 at 03:26:40Z. Traffic shift completed. Hitting canary checks.

Samir K.: p95/p99 trending down in us-west-2 already: p95 420ms -> 190ms, p99 1200ms -> 300ms. EU still elevated while rollback finishes.

Todd L.: rollback finished globally at 03:28:12Z. RB-314159-01 reports success. We also set `aggressive-batching=false` on dedicated pools for 10m window.

Samir K.: after rollback we still saw a handful of stragglers tied to in-flight long-context sessions. Kicking active connections causes some client retries; I pushed a soft-throttle to reduce concurrent long-context starts: `feature-flag set long-context-concurrency 0.2`

Jin Park: can confirm root cause hypothesis: the new dequant memcpy path uses a fused copy that under certain memory alignment and sequence lengths added blocking on host->device transfer. On some driver versions that surfaces as a 0.8-1.2s stall. We'll revert that optimization from calib-v2 and re-run calibration with extended long-context regression tests.

Nora (CS): customers report streams largely recovered. Maria updated CS-8674. Thanks.

Todd L.: monitoring for 20m before closing. Current cluster-wide metrics: p95=190ms, p99=320ms, error-rate down to 0.12%. No OOMs.

eng-runtime: created temporary incident tag and pinned graphs: https://dash.redwood.example/incident/3141598976/graphs

Samir K.: Followups: 1) revert fused memcpy optimization from calib-v2 2) extend long-context perf tests in CI and add driver matrix 3) add canary gating for calib profile rollouts that includes p99 streaming on >1024 seq synthetic traffic 4) document rollback steps in runbook. I’ll open PRs and assign.

Jin Park: PR for reverted change opened: PR#5421. Also adding a smoke test harness that replays 1k long-context streams into staging.

Todd L.: creating postmortem draft and tagging eng-runtime + eng-ml + oncall. Will attach timeline and customer impact summary.

Maria G.: CS to follow up with impacted customers with timeline and mitigation notes.

IncidentBot: Auto-check: 15m window passed, no alert re-fire. Alert remains resolved.

Todd L.: marking incident as mitigated. Will keep thread open until postmortem is ready. Great quick ops work. :thumbsup:

Nora (CS): closing loop with customers now. Thanks everyone.

Samir K.: assigning followups in tracker: TR-314159-calib-fix (owners: Samir, Jin).

Jin Park: postmortem link (draft): https://confluence.redwood.example/display/INC/3141598976-calib-burst-triage

Todd L.: last_check p95=185ms p99=310ms error-rate=0.09% — closing paging at 03:39:10Z.

Maria G.: CS updated ticket and sent customer notes.

IncidentBot: Incident closed by Todd L. at 2026-03-15T03:39:10Z.
